subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval while limiting anti-herd behavior to heartbeat and cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config shape, and repository policy treats config/default additions and scheduling surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design narrow every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit cron `every` phase or stagger contract with schema, CLI/RPC, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve fixed anchored `every` semantics and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept broader prime cadence
options.body: Add opt-in prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls across heartbeat and cron with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit cron `every` phase or stagger contract with schema, CLI/RPC, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current cron stagger controls and original scheduler surface, making them the strongest routing candidate for the cron scheduling product boundary.
